No candidate received a majority, so a runoff was held on August 18 between [[Aisha Wahab]] and Melissa Hernandez. The special election was conducted under "old boundaries" which were used in [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections in California#District 14|2022]] and [[2024 United States House of Representatives elections in California#District 14|2024]], while the full term [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in California (districts 1–26)#District 14|November 2026]] election will take place under new boundaries as a result of [[2025 California Proposition 50|Proposition 50]].{{Cite web |date=August 17, 2026 |title=What to expect in California’s special congressional election for Eric Swalwell's seat |url=https://www.kcra.com/article/california-14th-district-special-election-swalwell-seat/73453815 |access-date=October 2, 2026 |website=KCRA |language=en}} Wahab, a [[Progressivism in the United States|political progressive]], was seen as the favorite to win the runoff, while Hernandez received massive support from the [[Israel lobby in the United States|pro-Israel lobby]] in the closing days of the race.{{cite news |title=Aisha Wahab: AIPAC's latest target |first=Dustin |last=Gardiner |display-authors=etal |website=Politico |date=August 6, 2026 |access-date=August 20, 2026 |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/california-playbook/2026/08/06/aisha-wahab-aipacs-latest-target-01026765 |url-access=registration}} Wahab was declared the winner of the runoff on August 20, two days after election night, due to preliminary results being too close to call. She will serve the remainder of Swalwell's term in the [[119th United States Congress]].{{cite news |title=Progressive Overcomes AIPAC Opposition to Win Race to Replace Swalwell |first=Jennifer |last=Medina |website=The New York Times |date=August 20, 2026 |access-date=August 20, 2026 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/20/us/politics/wahab-hernandez-california-special-election.html}} == Background == Incumbent Representative Eric Swalwell did not seek re-election in 2026 and instead [[2026 California gubernatorial election|ran for governor of California]]. In April 2026, he faced allegations of sexual misconduct from several women.{{cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2026/04/10/us/eric-swalwell-sexual-misconduct-allegations-invs|title=Exclusive: Four women describe sexual misconduct by Rep. Eric Swalwell, including a former staffer who says he raped her|last=Walsh|first=Joe|date=April 10, 2026|access-date=April 13, 2026|website=[[CNN]]}} Amid growing calls for him to withdraw, he suspended his gubernatorial campaign on April 12.{{Cite news |last=Kuang |first=Jeanne |date=April 12, 2026 |title=Eric Swalwell suspends campaign for California governor after sex assault allegations |url=https://calmatters.org/politics/2026/04/california-governor-swalwell-out/ |access-date=April 15, 2026 |work=CalMatters |language=en-US}} The following day, he announced his pending resignation from Congress,{{cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/rep-eric-swalwell-of-california-says-he-will-resign-from-congress-after-sexual-assault-allegations|title=Rep. Eric Swalwell of California says he will resign from Congress after sexual assault allegations|last1=Freking|first1=Kevin|last2=Mascaro|first2=Lisa|last3=Cappelletti|first3=Joey|date=April 13, 2026|access-date=April 15, 2026|work=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=PBS}} which was filed and took effect on April 14.{{Cite web |date=April 14, 2026 |title=Reps. Tony Gonzales and Eric Swalwell officially resign amid misconduct claims |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/reps-tony-gonzales-eric-swalwell-officially-resign-misconduct-claims-rcna331765 |access-date=April 14, 2026 |website=[[NBC News]]}} Governor [[Gavin Newsom]] announced on April 14 that the special election would be held on August 18,{{Cite web |date=April 14, 2026 |title=Governor Newsom issues proclamation setting special election for California Congressional District 14 |url=https://www.gov.ca.gov/2026/04/14/governor-newsom-issues-proclamation-setting-special-election-for-california-congressional-district-14/ |access-date=April 14, 2026 |website=Governor of California |language=en}} but California special election rules state that the first round would be held on the ninth preceding Tuesday, June 16.{{Cite web |date=April 14, 2026 | title=Congressional District 14, Special Primary Election Calendar |url=https://elections.cdn.sos.ca.gov/special-elections/2026-cd14/primary-calendar.pdf |access-date=August 12, 2026 |website=California Secretary of State}} Over half of the unofficial candidates in the special election also filed to run in the [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in California#District 14|regularly-scheduled election for California's 14th congressional district]]. April 23 was the filing deadline for candidates in the special election.{{cite web|url=https://www.pleasantonweekly.com/election/2026/04/21/candidates-line-up-for-congressional-district-14-special-election/|title=Candidates line up for Congressional District 14 special election|last=Strzemp|first=Jude|date=April 21, 2026|access-date=April 24, 2026|website=[[Pleasanton Weekly]]}} In April 2026, regional [[California Democratic Party|Democratic]] leaders attempted to broker a "caretaker" agreement to avoid an August runoff. The goal was to secure a swift victory by clearing the candidate field for former State Senator [[Bob Wieckowski]] to serve as a placeholder for the rest of Swalwell's term. However, he made it clear he would only run if he received a unanimous endorsement from all major contenders.{{Cite web |last=Mason |first=Melanie |last2=Jones |first2=Blake |date=April 20, 2026 |title=California Dems want to quickly fill Swalwell’s seat. They’re hitting a snag. |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2026/04/20/california-dems-swalwell-seat-00882425 |url-status=live |archive-url= |archive-date= |website=[[Politico]]}} The agreement fell apart when [[Aisha Wahab]] refused to sign on. Party leaders, including Representative [[Zoe Lofgren]], had pushed the deal in hopes that a single unified candidate could clear the 50% threshold. Lofgren argued that the narrow margins in the House necessitated full representation to prevent crucial legislation from hypothetically failing by a single vote.{{Cite web |last=Martin |first=Kyle |date=April 24, 2026 |title=Democratic plan to quickly fill Swalwell seat collapses, setting up crowded race |url=https://www.marinij.com/2026/04/24/democratic-plan-to-quickly-fill-swalwell-seat-collapses-setting-up-crowded-race/ |url-status=live |website=Marin Independent Journal}} Various candidates who ran for the special election also ran in the regularly-scheduled election, including Wahab, Melissa Hernandez, Wendy Huang, Dena Maldonado, Rakhi Israni Singh and Tom Wong.{{Cite news |last=Strzemp |first=Jude |date=April 27, 2026|access-date=June 17, 2026|website=[[Pleasanton Weekly]] |title=Ballot finalized for Congressional District 14 special election |url=https://www.pleasantonweekly.com/regional-politics/2026/04/27/ballot-finalized-for-congressional-district-14-special-election/ |url-status=live}} ==Candidates== === Advanced to runoff ===
